findings.title: Attachment-section overhead isn't charged to the budget, so fitTask can truncate the diff
findings.detail: The headroom that bounds attachments is `TASK_MAX_BYTES - skeleton - chunkText(i) - 2048`, and `selectAttachments` only counts each file's `content` bytes (`size` is `Buffer.byteLength(piece.content)`). It does not count the section framing that `renderAttachments` adds: the ~200-byte `## Current contents of the changed files` header plus a `### <path> (<label>)` line per attached file. `budget = min(attachChars, headroom)` is consumed by content bytes alone, so with many small changed files the greedy smallest-first pack attaches all of them and the framing overhead can exceed the 2048 margin. Example: a chunk of ~900 one-to-few-byte files (chunkChars 96k, so a chunk can hold hundreds of `diff --git` headers) yields a few KB of content but tens of KB of `### path` headers, pushing `skeleton + chunkText + attachments` past `TASK_MAX_BYTES`. `fitTask` then falls into its truncation branch and cuts the diff — directly contradicting the documented contract 'attachments never shrink the diff (they use only task-cap headroom)' in the README and the stage 0e comment. The finder is told the diff is partial, but coverage silently shrinks exactly where the review is granular.
findings.recommendation: Charge the rendered section overhead to the budget: subtract the header/heading bytes (or a per-file overhead per entry) from headroom before selecting, and/or verify Buffer.byteLength(renderAttachments(...)) <= headroom and drop attachable files until it fits.

findings.title: Attachments read changed files by path with fs.readFile (follows symlinks) and ship whole working-tree contents to the remote model
findings.detail: The new Stage 0e loop reads each changed file's current contents with `deps.readFile(path.join(repoRoot, f.path))` and embeds the result in the finder task, which is passed to a child process that prompts the configured remote model (default `opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash:off`). Two exposures: (1) `deps.readFile` is a plain `fs.readFile` (see reviewDeps at line ~1662), which follows symlinks. Git tracks symlinks as mode-120000 entries whose diff contains only the link target and a one-line hunk, so `hunkRanges` yields a range and `sliceAttachment` (which attaches the *whole file* when the window covers it) causes the symlink's target file to be read and sent — e.g. a tracked `config/link -> /etc/passwd` or `-> ~/.ssh/id_rsa` in the changed set exfiltrates that file's contents to the model provider, content that is not in the diff the user chose to review. (2) For ordinary changed files the attachment carries the full current file (small file) or ±40-line windows (large file), i.e. unchanged regions that may hold secrets; `isExcludedPath` (line 281) only filters lockfiles/logs/generated/binary paths and does not cover `.env`/credential files, so whole secret-bearing files are uploaded. The budget/byte-cap logic correctly prevents overrun but does not restrict *what* is read. Note the eval harness is safe (`readFile: async () => undefined` in scripts/eval-review.ts:220), so this concerns production `/review` runs on a real working tree.
findings.recommendation: Use `lstat` and skip non-regular files (symlinks) before reading, or read with `fs.open`/`O_NOFOLLOW` and reject targets that resolve outside `repoRoot`; additionally extend `isExcludedPath` (or add a dedicated allow/deny list) to cover secret-bearing paths (e.g. `.env*`, `*.pem`, `*.key`, `id_*`) so whole-file attachment cannot upload credentials the diff did not include.

findings.title: Turn-economy prompt asserts attachments exist even when attaching is disabled
findings.detail: TURN_ECONOMY_RULES unconditionally tells every finder 'The changed files' current contents are already attached; do not re-read what you have.' When PI_REVIEW_ATTACH_CHARS=0 (documented as disabling) or a file was skipped/oversized, no content is attached (and with 0 the skipped note never appears either), so the instruction tells the finder to avoid re-reading files it does not possess — pushing it toward answering from a diff alone, contradicting the attachment design. This rule is rendered into finderAgent instructions for every lens regardless of config.
findings.recommendation: Make the 'do not re-read' sentence conditional on attachments being present (e.g. only add that line when the rendered attachment section will be included), or reword it to describe the reference material without asserting it is always present.

findings.title: mergeRanges clamps start only above 1, producing empty reversed windows
findings.detail: The docstring promises clamping to [1, maxLine], but start is clamped only with Math.max(1, r.start - width) (line 1154) while end uses Math.min(maxLine, r.end + width) (line 1155). If a hunk's new-side start exceeds the current file's line count, start' > end'. That happens with a `range v1..v2` target (or ref target) when the working tree has fewer lines than the diff's head — e.g. later commits removed lines — so hunkRanges returns start=460 for a 100-line file and mergeRanges yields {start:360, end:100}. sliceAttachment then renders an empty slice with the reversed label `lines 360-100`; because piece is non-null the file is neither attached correctly nor listed in the skipped note, so the finder sees a bogus empty window.
findings.recommendation: Clamp start to Math.min(maxLine, Math.max(1, r.start - width)) and discard any range whose end < start before slicing.

findings.title: The 'attachments never shrink the diff' guarantee is only tested on a tiny diff; the over-cap path is untested
findings.detail: The new feature's documented invariant (README: 'attachments never shrink the diff (they use only task-cap headroom)'; extensions/review.ts:1461-1466) rests on `headroom = TASK_MAX_BYTES - skeleton(lens 0) - chunkText - 2048`, with `budget = min(attachChars, headroom)`. Only review.test.ts:276 asserts the byte cap, and it runs SAMPLE_DIFF (2 files, ~1KB) with default attachChars, so headroom is ~115KB and the assertion is trivially true. No test drives the boundary where headroom is the binding constraint or is <= 0 (the `if (budget <= 0) continue` branch at extensions/review.ts:1466), so a regression that lets attachments push the task over TASK_MAX_BYTES and causes fitTask to truncate the diff would still pass. The headroom also ignores the bytes renderAttachments adds on top of the measured content sizes — the preamble line, each `### <path> (label)` header and the `\n\n` separators — so the rendered section can exceed `budget` by that overhead; with many small files in one chunk under a large diff, the 2048 margin can be consumed and the diff truncated. That accounting/edge interaction is exactly what no test covers.
findings.recommendation: Add a test using a large chunk text plus several small attachable files (attachChars below headroom) that asserts the finder task still contains the complete `## The diff` (not the 'diff truncated' note) and stays <= TASK_MAX_BYTES; include header/preamble bytes in the headroom calculation.

findings.title: PI_REVIEW_CONCURRENCY parsing/clamping has no test, unlike the sibling knobs
findings.detail: The new `concurrency` knob is parsed at extensions/review.ts:157 via `clampInt(env.PI_REVIEW_CONCURRENCY, 8, 1, 16)`, but its only test is the default assertion at tests/review.test.ts:469. The override/clamp test (the same block that asserts PI_REVIEW_CHUNK_CHARS clamps to 8_000, PI_REVIEW_ATTACH_CHARS to 262_144, PI_REVIEW_MAX_CHILDREN to 32, etc.) never sets PI_REVIEW_CONCURRENCY, and the blank-value test that guards the sibling knobs does not include it either. A regression in the min/max bounds (1..16) or the blank-as-unset handling for this knob would not be caught.
findings.recommendation: Add PI_REVIEW_CONCURRENCY overrides (over max, under min, and blank) to the existing clamp/blank parse tests and assert the resulting values.
